title: An abelian group is injective exactly when it is divisible
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises the injective objects of the category of abelian groups: an abelian group is injective if and only if it is divisible, meaning that every equation n y = x is solvable (statement lines 13552-13556). The proof is the longest of the section at 46 lines (proof lines 13559-13604) and it has two halves. For the necessity, a failure of divisibility produces an element x and an integer n such that the map Z to J sending m to m x does not extend to the group Z[1/n], which exhibits the failure of injectivity. For the sufficiency, one applies Zorn's lemma to the set of partial extensions of a given map A to J, verifies that chains have upper bounds by glueing, and then shows that a maximal partial extension is defined on all of B by picking x outside its domain and treating the two cases: if no positive multiple of x lies in the domain, one extends by mapping x to any element; if a minimal n with n x in the domain exists, divisibility of J supplies z with n z = phi(n x), and the map on the direct sum of the domain with Z given by (a, m) to phi(a) + m z factors through the subgroup generated by the domain and x. Both halves are carried out completely, and the two case splits are where the divisibility hypothesis is consumed.
